mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS indicates labor market strength that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Payrolls momentum does not correlate with SPX 20-day returns (Spearman's rho < 0.2) in the 30-day window following the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (GDPC1) suggests weakening aggregate demand, which typically precedes a short-term pullback in S&P 500 forward expectations over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 5% from the prior quarter
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 5-day average during confirmed demand contractions (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in the INDP supply index below 100 signals tight supply conditions that can drive risk-on sentiment and higher S&P 500 forward pricing over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 and remains below for 2 months
failure_condition: No significant positive return in SPX 20-day forward when INDP remains below 100 for at least 3 months (t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it indicates a labor market shift that lowers real discount rates, supporting equity valuation expansion and positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% and remains below for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with UNRATE changes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising HOUST (household spending) suggests pent-up demand that translates into higher S&P 500 expectations over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 10% from the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not higher than the prior 20-day average during confirmed acceleration (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE below their 2021 averages creates a dual pressure that reduces discounting of future cash flows and weakens labor-cost expectations, jointly pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.5% AND UNRATE < 4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from a baseline of no policy/labor change (p > 0.05) during the interaction window.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis recovery regime (defined by CPIAUCSL < 280 and GDPC1 > 19000), S&P 500 forward returns tend to be positive over the next 5 days as market participants anticipate sustained economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 280 AND GDPC1 > 19000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In the identified regime, SPX 5-day forward returns are not positive in more than 60% of instances (binomial test, p > 0.05).
